q: Which club beat Watford 6-0 in the 2019 FA Cup final?
sub: Gabriel Jesus and Raheem Sterling both scored twice.
note: Confirmed on the 2019 final page: City 6-0, Silva 26, Jesus 38 and 68, De Bruyne 61, Sterling 81 and 87. Both braces check out. No duplicate in the shipping file.

q: By the end of the 2024-25 season, which club had won the FA Cup more times than any other?
sub: Fourteen, the last of them in 2020.
note: FA Cup page: Arsenal 14, last in 2020, ahead of Manchester United. Record is anchored to a closed season, so it passes the shelf-life rule.

q: Which club beat Manchester City 1-0 in the 2025 FA Cup final to win their first major trophy?
sub: Eberechi Eze scored in the 16th minute.
note: 2025 final page: Eze 16th minute, 1-0, first major trophy excluding the defunct Full Members' Cup of 1991.

q: Which club won the FA Cup for the first time in 2021, beating Chelsea 1-0 at Wembley?
sub: They had lost all four of their previous finals.
note: 2021 final page confirms first FA Cup and four previous finals all lost, the last in 1969. Venue Wembley, crowd capped at 20,000.

q: In which city were the FA Cup finals played from 2001 to 2006, while Wembley was being rebuilt?
sub: At the Millennium Stadium.
note: Finals list and the FA Cup page both give 2001 to 2006 at the Millennium Stadium, with 2000 the last at the old Wembley and 2007 the first at the new one.

q: Which club won the 2020 FA Cup final 2-1 against Chelsea, in an empty Wembley?
sub: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored both goals.
note: 2020 final page: Pulisic 5, Aubameyang 28 penalty and 67, played behind closed doors in August 2020.

q: What is the English season-opening match between the league champions and the FA Cup holders called?
sub: It was the Charity Shield until the name changed in 2002.
note: Community Shield page confirms champions against FA Cup holders, season curtain-raiser, renamed from Charity Shield in 2002.

q: Which club won the 2025 League Cup final, their first major domestic trophy since 1955?
sub: They beat Liverpool 2-1 at Wembley.
note: 2025 EFL Cup final page: Newcastle 2-1 Liverpool at Wembley, first major domestic trophy since the 1954-55 FA Cup. The domestic qualifier is needed because of the 1969 Fairs Cup.

q: Which club beat Manchester City 2-1 in the 2024 FA Cup final?
sub: Alejandro Garnacho and Kobbie Mainoo scored.
note: 2024 final page: Garnacho 30, Mainoo 39, Doku 87. Same scoreline as 2023 but the other way round, so the year matters and it is right here.

q: Which energy drink brand took over the naming of the League Cup in 2017?
sub: A Thai brand, hence the Carabao Cup.
note: Fact confirmed (Carabao from 2017-18, deal now running to 2029), but the wording was a live present-tense claim, which the brief throws out. Reworded to a closed event in 2017.

q: Which club won the 2023 FA Cup final, the first to be contested by both Manchester clubs?
sub: City went on to complete the treble that season.
note: Result and first all-Manchester final confirmed (City 2-1, Gundogan 1 and 51, Fernandes 33 pen). Old sub named Gundogan's brace, which is the answer to the hard row later in this file, so it was swapped for the treble to kill the leak.

q: Which Arsenal manager won seven FA Cups, the last of them in 2017?
note: 2017 final page calls Wenger the most successful manager in the competition with seven wins. The finals list bears it out: 1998, 2002, 2003, 2005, 2014, 2015, 2017.

q: Which club did Chelsea beat 1-0 in the 2018 FA Cup final?
sub: Eden Hazard scored a penalty.
note: Finals list: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester United, Wembley 2018. Hazard's penalty is the only goal.

q: Which club won the 2014 FA Cup final 3-2 against Hull City after extra time?
sub: They had been 2-0 down inside nine minutes.
note: 2014 final page: Chester 4, Davies 8, Cazorla 17, Koscielny 71, Ramsey 109. Extra time and the early two-goal hole both check out.

q: Which club won the 2012 FA Cup final, beating Liverpool 2-1 at Wembley?
sub: Ramires and Didier Drogba scored.
note: 2012 final page: Ramires 11, Drogba 52, Carroll 64. Wembley, May 2012.

q: Which south coast club won the 2008 FA Cup final under Harry Redknapp?
sub: Their first FA Cup since 1939, and Redknapp's first trophy.
note: 2008 final page: Portsmouth 1-0 Cardiff, Kanu 37, first FA Cup since 1939, and the first major trophy of Redknapp's 25-year managerial career.

q: Which club beat Bradford City 5-0 in the 2013 League Cup final?
sub: Bradford were a League Two side, three divisions below Swansea.
note: Result right (Swansea 5-0, Wembley, 24 Feb 2013). The sub was wrong: Bradford were in League Two at the time of the final and only won promotion through the play-offs that May, so they had not come up from it. Rewritten.

q: Which club won the 2004 League Cup, the first major trophy in their history?
sub: Steve McClaren's side beat Bolton 2-1 in Cardiff.
note: 2004 final page: Middlesbrough 2-1 Bolton at the Millennium Stadium under McClaren, the club's first major trophy in 128 years.

q: Who scored the only goal of the 2011 FA Cup final, Manchester City's first trophy in 35 years?
sub: A 74th minute finish past Thomas Sorensen of Stoke.
note: 2011 final page: Toure 74th minute past Sorensen, City's first major trophy for 35 years.

q: Which club did Chelsea beat 2-0 in the 1997 FA Cup final?
note: 1997 final page: Chelsea 2-0 Middlesbrough, Di Matteo 43 seconds and Newton 83.

q: Which club beat Arsenal 2-1 in the 2011 League Cup final, then known as the Carling Cup?
note: Final page: Birmingham 2-1 Arsenal, Zigic 28, Van Persie 39, Martins 89. Carling was the sponsor from 2003 to 2012, so the 2010-11 edition is right.

q: Which club did Chelsea beat 1-0 in the 2000 FA Cup final, the last played at the old Wembley?
sub: Roberto Di Matteo scored again.
note: 1999-2000 FA Cup page: Chelsea 1-0 Aston Villa on 20 May 2000, Di Matteo the scorer, and the finals list shows the move to Cardiff from 2001, so it was the last at the old ground.

q: Which club beat Chelsea 4-0 in the 1994 FA Cup final to complete their first league and cup double?
note: Fact confirmed (United 4-0, Cantona two penalties, Hughes, McClair, and their first double). The src pointed at the 1996 final page, which is a different match, so it was corrected to 1994.

q: Which club beat Manchester United 1-0 in the 1995 FA Cup final?
note: Finals list: Everton 1-0 Manchester United, Wembley 1995.

q: Which club did Arsenal beat 2-1 in the 2017 FA Cup final?
note: 2017 final page: Sanchez 4, Costa 76, Ramsey 79, Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea.

q: Liverpool won both domestic cups in 2021-22, beating the same club on penalties in both finals. Which club?
note: Both finals lists confirm it: League Cup 0-0 and 11-10 on penalties in February 2022, FA Cup 0-0 and 6-5 on penalties in May 2022, Chelsea on the losing end twice.

q: Liverpool won three cups in 2000-01. Which three were they?
a: The FA Cup, the League Cup and the UEFA Cup
note: Season page: League Cup (Birmingham, 5-4 on penalties), FA Cup (Arsenal 2-1), UEFA Cup (Alaves 5-4). All three belong to 2000-01 even though all three finals fell in 2001.

q: Which Frenchman managed Liverpool to their cup treble in 2000-01?
note: Season page names Houllier as manager for the treble season.

q: Newcastle United lost the FA Cup final two years running, 1998 and 1999. Who beat them?
a: Arsenal in 1998 and Manchester United in 1999
sub: Both finals finished 2-0.
note: Facts confirmed on the finals list: Arsenal 2-0 in 1998, Manchester United 2-0 in 1999. Only the wording changed, dropping a stray 'in' that made the line trip when read aloud.

q: Which club did Chelsea beat 1-0 in the 2010 FA Cup final, completing the double?
sub: Didier Drogba scored the free kick.
note: 2010 final page: Drogba's 59th minute free kick, 1-0 against Portsmouth, and Chelsea had taken the league the week before, so the double stands.

q: Which club won the 2009 FA Cup final 2-1 against Everton?
sub: Didier Drogba and Frank Lampard scored.
note: 2009 final page: Saha 25 seconds for Everton, then Drogba 21 and Lampard 72.

q: Which club won the Premier League, the FA Cup and the League Cup all in 2018-19?
note: Season page confirms the domestic treble: league on 12 May, FA Cup on 18 May, League Cup on 24 February.

q: By what sponsored name was the League Cup known from 2003 to 2012?
note: EFL Cup page sponsorship table: Carling 2003 to 2012, between Worthington and Capital One.

q: Which club won the 2007 FA Cup final, the first played at the new Wembley?
sub: Didier Drogba beat Manchester United in extra time.
note: 2007 final page: first final at the new Wembley, Drogba on 116 minutes, 1-0 after extra time.

q: Which Manchester United manager was sacked days after winning the 2016 FA Cup final?
sub: Jose Mourinho was appointed six days after the final.
note: Sacking confirmed, but the old sub was wrong. Van Gaal's page says he went two days after the 21 May final and the final's page says five, while both agree Mourinho arrived on 27 May, so it was not the day after. Sub now anchors to the one date the sources share.

q: Which club did Arsenal beat 4-0 in the 2015 FA Cup final?
note: Finals list: Arsenal 4-0 Aston Villa, Wembley 2015.

q: Which club did Arsenal beat 1-0 in the 2003 FA Cup final?
note: Finals list: Arsenal 1-0 Southampton at the Millennium Stadium in 2003.

q: Which club did Manchester United beat 4-0 in the 2006 League Cup final?
note: League Cup finals list: Manchester United 4-0 Wigan at the Millennium Stadium in 2006.

q: Which club did Liverpool beat 2-0 in the 2003 League Cup final?
note: League Cup finals list: Liverpool 2-0 Manchester United, 2003, part of the Worthington Cup era.

q: Which club beat Bolton Wanderers 2-1 in the 1995 League Cup final?
note: League Cup finals list: Liverpool 2-1 Bolton at Wembley, 1995, then the Coca-Cola Cup.

q: Who scored Leicester City's winner in the 1997 League Cup final replay at Hillsborough?
sub: In the 100th minute against Middlesbrough.
note: Final page: 1-1 after extra time on 6 April, replay at Hillsborough on 16 April, Claridge in the 100th minute. Both the replay and the minute hold up.

q: Who scored Arsenal's winner in the last minutes of extra time in the 1993 FA Cup final replay?
sub: Ian Wright had scored the other.
note: 1993 final page: replay 2-1, Wright 34, Waddle deflection 68, Linighan heads it in on 119 from a Merson corner, with a broken nose. Replay and timing both right.

q: Arsenal won both domestic cups in 1992-93. Which club did they beat in both finals?
sub: 2-1 in the League Cup, then 2-1 in an FA Cup final replay.
note: Both finals lists agree: League Cup 2-1 and FA Cup 1-1 then 2-1 in the replay, Sheffield Wednesday beaten twice.

q: Who scored the winning penalty in the 2005 FA Cup final shootout against Manchester United?
sub: His last kick for Arsenal, in the first final decided on penalties.
note: 2005 final page: 0-0, the first FA Cup final to go to penalties, Vieira with the decisive kick in what was his last match for Arsenal before Juventus.

q: The 2006 FA Cup final, Liverpool against West Ham, is remembered by whose name?
sub: 3-3, then 3-1 on penalties, with Gerrard scoring twice.
note: 2006 final page: 3-3 after extra time, Gerrard 54 and 90+1, Liverpool 3-1 on penalties.

q: Who scored twice late on for Liverpool to beat Arsenal 2-1 in the 2001 FA Cup final?
note: 2001 final page: Ljungberg 72, Owen 83 and 88, at the Millennium Stadium.

q: Who scored Manchester United's 85th minute winner against Liverpool in the 1996 FA Cup final?
sub: It sealed United's second double.
note: 1996 final page: Cantona on 85, 1-0, and the page states United became the first club to do the double twice.

q: Who scored Arsenal's extra-time winner against Hull City in the 2014 FA Cup final?
note: 2014 final page: Ramsey on 109 from Giroud's backheel, 3-2 after extra time.

q: Who headed Wigan Athletic's injury-time winner in the 2013 FA Cup final?
sub: From a Shaun Maloney corner.
note: 2013 final page: Watson heads in a Maloney corner on 90+1, after Zabaleta had been sent off on 84. Injury time and the header both correct.

q: Who scored Portsmouth's winner in the 2008 FA Cup final against Cardiff City?
note: 2008 final page: Kanu on 37, the only goal of the match.

q: Which goalkeeper played for Manchester United in the 2009 League Cup final shootout win over Tottenham?
sub: He took the man of the match award.
note: 2009 final page: 0-0 after extra time, United 4-1 on penalties, Foster the first keeper since Dudek in 2003 to take the Alan Hardaker Award.

q: Who scored Tottenham's extra-time winner in the 2008 League Cup final against Chelsea?
sub: A header off Petr Cech and back onto his head.
note: 2008 final page: Drogba 39, Berbatov 70 penalty, Woodgate 94. He headed a Jenas free kick onto Cech and it came back onto his head.

q: Which club beat Tottenham 2-1 in the 2002 League Cup final, then known as the Worthington Cup?
note: Finals list: Blackburn 2-1 Tottenham at the Millennium Stadium, and the EFL Cup page puts Worthington from 1998 to 2003, so the sponsor name is right for the 2001-02 edition.

q: Matt Elliott scored twice for Leicester City in the 2000 League Cup final. Which club did they beat?
note: 2000 final page: Elliott 29 and 81, Kelly 77 for Tranmere, Leicester 2-1. Kept in preference to the extreme row later in this file, which asked the same final from the other end.

q: Who scored Birmingham City's 89th minute winner in the 2011 League Cup final against Arsenal?
note: Final page: Martins on 89 after the Szczesny and Koscielny mix-up, Birmingham 2-1.

q: Which club beat Manchester United 3-1 in the 1994 League Cup final?
note: Finals list: Aston Villa 3-1 Manchester United at Wembley, 1994.

q: Which Chelsea player was sent off in the 2017 FA Cup final?
sub: Booked a second time for diving in the box.
note: 2017 final page: Moses off on 68 for a second yellow, given for going down in the Arsenal box. Only dismissal in the match, so the answer is unique.

q: Which Manchester United defender was sent off in extra time in the 2016 FA Cup final?
note: 2016 final page: Smalling off on 105 for a second yellow on Bolasie, the fourth player ever dismissed in an FA Cup final. Extra time is correct, since 105 is the end of the first extra period.

q: Who scored both Manchester City goals in the 2023 FA Cup final against Manchester United?
note: 2023 final page: Gundogan 1 and 51, Fernandes 33 penalty. The opener came after 12 seconds, the fastest in a final. Kept because the easy row's sub was rewritten to stop giving this away.

q: Who scored Chelsea's opening goal in the 2020 FA Cup final against Arsenal?
note: 2020 final page: Pulisic on 5, before Aubameyang's two.

q: Who scored the only goal of the 2021 FA Cup final for Leicester City?
sub: A strike from distance in the 63rd minute.
note: 2021 final page: Tielemans on 63, 1-0 against Chelsea.

q: Which two players scored for Newcastle United in the 2025 League Cup final?
note: 2025 final page: Burn 45 from a Trippier corner, Isak 52, Chiesa 90+4 for Liverpool.

q: Which club chose not to defend the FA Cup in 1999-2000, going to the Club World Championship instead?
sub: The first FA Cup winners not to defend the trophy.
note: 1999-2000 FA Cup page confirms the withdrawal for the 2000 Club World Championship in Brazil and calls them the first holders not to defend the trophy.

q: Who was Millwall's player-manager when they lost the 2004 FA Cup final to Manchester United?
sub: Millwall were tenth in the First Division that season.
note: 2004 final page: Wise was player-manager and played in the match, Millwall finished tenth in the First Division, United won 3-0.

q: Who scored both Chelsea goals in the 2007 League Cup final against Arsenal?
sub: Theo Walcott had put Arsenal ahead.
note: 2007 final page: Walcott 12, Drogba 20 and 84, Chelsea 2-1 at the Millennium Stadium.

q: Where was the 2007 League Cup final played, three months before the new Wembley hosted the FA Cup final?
sub: The seventh and last League Cup final held there.
note: Final page: 25 February 2007 at the Millennium Stadium, and it says in so many words that this was the seventh and last League Cup final there. The FA Cup final followed on 19 May at the new Wembley, so the gap is right.

q: Which ground hosted the 2012 Community Shield, with Wembley staging the Olympic football final?
sub: Manchester City beat Chelsea 3-2 there.
note: 2012 Community Shield page: Villa Park because Wembley had the Olympic football final that weekend, City 3-2 (Toure, Tevez, Nasri against Torres and Bertrand).

q: Which ground hosted the 2022 Community Shield, with Wembley staging the Women's Euro final?
sub: Liverpool beat Manchester City 3-1 in Leicester.
note: 2022 Community Shield page: King Power Stadium because of the Women's Euro final at Wembley, Liverpool 3-1 (Alexander-Arnold, Salah, Nunez against Alvarez).

q: Which club did League Two side Bradford City beat on penalties in the 2012-13 League Cup quarter-final?
sub: 1-1 at Valley Parade, then 3-2 in the shootout.
note: Bradford's 2012-13 season page: 11 December 2012 at Valley Parade, 1-1 after extra time, Bradford 3-2 on penalties, and they were a fourth-tier side. Season label 2012-13 is right for a December tie.

q: Which Championship club knocked Chelsea and Arsenal out of the 2008-09 League Cup?
sub: Tottenham beat them in the semi-finals.
note: Competition page: Burnley beat Chelsea 5-4 on penalties in round four and Arsenal 2-0 in round five, then lost 6-4 on aggregate to Tottenham in the semis while in the Championship.

q: Which non-league club reached the 2017 FA Cup quarter-finals after winning at Burnley?
sub: The first non-league side in the quarters since 1914.
note: Match page: fifth round, Raggett on 89, Lincoln of the National League the first non-league club in the last eight in 103 years, since QPR in 1914.

q: Barnsley beat Liverpool and Chelsea in the 2007-08 FA Cup. Who beat them in the semi-final?
sub: Joe Ledley scored after nine minutes at Wembley.
note: 2007-08 FA Cup page: 2-1 at Anfield in round five, 1-0 against Chelsea at Oakwell in round six, then 0-1 to Cardiff at Wembley on 6 April with Ledley scoring in the 9th minute.

q: Which League Two club beat Newcastle United 3-1 in the FA Cup third round in January 2011?
sub: Stevenage were in their first season in the Football League.
note: Result confirmed on both the Stevenage and Newcastle 2010-11 season pages: 3-1 at Broadhall Way, Stevenage a League Two club in their first Football League season. Neither page records any red card, so the Cheick Tiote claim in the sub could not be stood up and was replaced.

q: Who scored the penalty that knocked Manchester United out of the 2007-08 FA Cup at Old Trafford?
sub: Portsmouth won the quarter-final 1-0 and went on to win the cup.
note: 2007-08 FA Cup page: sixth round at Old Trafford on 8 March 2008, Muntari's penalty on 78, Portsmouth 1-0 and later winners.

q: Whose penalty did Peter Schmeichel save in the 1999 FA Cup semi-final replay between Arsenal and Manchester United?
note: 1998-99 FA Cup page: the first meeting was a 0-0 draw with no penalty, and the save came in the replay on 14 April, in normal time, before Giggs won it on 109. Added 'replay' so the question points at the right match.

q: Which Manchester United player was sent off in the 1999 FA Cup semi-final replay against Arsenal?
sub: Ryan Giggs then won it in extra time.
note: 1998-99 FA Cup page: Keane off for a second yellow on Overmars in the replay, Giggs' solo goal on 109. Already says replay, so it is right as written.

q: Who scored for Chelsea after 43 seconds of the 1997 FA Cup final, a record for a final at the old Wembley?
note: 1997 final page: 43 seconds, the quickest goal in an FA Cup final at Wembley at the time, beating Jackie Milburn's 1955 mark. The old Wembley qualifier keeps it true despite Saha in 2009 and Gundogan in 2023.

q: Who scored after 25 seconds of the 2009 FA Cup final, then the fastest goal in a final at Wembley?
sub: For Everton against Chelsea, who still won 2-1.
note: 25 seconds and the 2-1 defeat are confirmed, but 'a record at the time' is contested because the page also points to Bob Chatt's 1895 goal. Pinned it to Wembley finals, where Saha's was the fastest until 2023, so there is one defensible reading.

q: Which two players scored for Middlesbrough in the 2004 League Cup final?
sub: Both inside the first seven minutes.
note: 2004 final page: Job on 2, Zenden's penalty on 7, Davies 21 for Bolton. The seven minute claim holds.

q: By what sponsored name was the League Cup known from 1992 to 1998?
note: EFL Cup sponsorship table: Coca-Cola 1992 to 1998, between Rumbelows and Worthington.

q: By what sponsored name was the League Cup known from 2012 to 2016?
note: EFL Cup sponsorship table: Capital One 2012 to 2016, then one unsponsored season as the EFL Cup before Carabao.

q: Which club won the last League Cup final played at the old Wembley, in 2000?
sub: 2-1 against Tranmere Rovers.
note: Duplicate. This is a mirror of the hard row 'Matt Elliott scored twice for Leicester City in the 2000 League Cup final. Which club did they beat?': one asks the winner and names Tranmere in the sub, the other names Leicester and asks for Tranmere. The facts are right (34th and last League Cup final at the old Wembley, Leicester 2-1), but only one of the pair can ship and the Elliott row is the better question.

q: By the end of the 2024-25 season, which club had won the League Cup most often?
sub: The tenth came in 2024 against Chelsea.
note: EFL Cup page: Liverpool ten, Manchester City nine, and the finals list confirms the tenth was 1-0 against Chelsea after extra time in 2024. Tier moved from extreme to hard: the record holder is standard serious-fan knowledge rather than anorak territory, and this deck is short of low tiers.

q: Which club beat Chelsea 4-2 at Stamford Bridge in the FA Cup fourth round in January 2015 after going 2-0 down?
sub: They were a League One side at the time.
note: Match page: 2014-15 FA Cup fourth round at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea 2-0 up through Cahill and Ramires inside 38 minutes, Bradford of League One won 4-2. Reworded from 'the 2015 FA Cup' to the calendar date, since the competition was the 2014-15 edition.

q: Who put through his own net to give West Ham the lead in the 2006 FA Cup final?
note: 2006 final page: Carragher turns Etherington's low cross into his own net on 21 for West Ham's first, then Ashton 28 and Konchesky 64.

q: Steve Morrow scored Arsenal's winner in the 1993 League Cup final and broke his arm celebrating. Who dropped him?
sub: He got his medal before the FA Cup final a month later.
note: 1993 final page: Morrow on 68 after Merson's equaliser, Adams slipped while lifting him, broken arm, straight to hospital, medal presented before the FA Cup final the following month.

q: Liverpool beat Cardiff City on penalties in the 2012 League Cup final. Which Cardiff player missed the last one?
sub: Cousin of Liverpool's Steven Gerrard, who was on the pitch.
note: 2012 final page: 2-2 after extra time at Wembley, Liverpool 3-2 on penalties, Anthony Gerrard missed the last kick and is named as Steven Gerrard's cousin.

q: Which Chelsea goalkeeper refused to be substituted in the 2019 League Cup final, leaving Maurizio Sarri raging?
sub: Antonio Rudiger had to hold Sarri back. Chelsea lost on penalties.
note: 2019 final page: Sarri tried to bring Caballero on late in extra time, Kepa stayed put, and Rudiger, who played in the match, held Sarri back. City won the shootout 4-3, so the sub is right on both counts.

q: Who scored a hat-trick for Leeds United against Liverpool in the 1992 Charity Shield, then joined Manchester United?
sub: Leeds won 4-3. He crossed the Pennines in November.
note: 1992 Charity Shield page: Leeds 4-3, Cantona 26, 77 and 87 plus man of the match. The November move to Old Trafford is not on that page but is not in dispute.

q: Which Crystal Palace goalkeeper saved a penalty and then the rebound in the 2025 FA Cup final?
sub: He stopped Omar Marmoush, then blocked Erling Haaland's follow-up.
note: 2025 final page: Mitchell fouled Bernardo Silva on 36, Marmoush's penalty saved by Henderson, Haaland's follow-up saved too. The sub matches the sequence.
